entries.text: Highlights This patch release fixes the dev server's Web UI loading as a blank page in Chrome 158 and later (stable from 2026-11-17), and fixes reported vulnerabilities in the CLI's dependencies. It has no command, flag or output changes. Users of temporal server start-dev should upgrade before Chrome 158 reaches them. Fixed temporal server start-dev Web UI no longer loads as a blank page in Chrome 158+. The bundled Web UI moves from v2.56.1 to v2.56.4, whose Content Security Policy uses script-src 'self' instead of 'strict-dynamic'. Chrome 158 blocks the UI's startup script imports under the old policy. (temporalio/ui#4126; #1260, #1267) Dependency updates fix the following reported vulnerabilities: Dependency Version Fixes Go standard library 1.26.11 CVE-2026-97054 (net/http server crash) github.com/klauspost/compress v1.20.4 CVE-2026-116591 (high) github.com/labstack/echo/v4 v4.16.4 CVE-2026-118651, CVE-2026-118653, GHSA-3f6j-cw5h-qw9c The two echo CVEs had no fix when v1.10.0 shipped. They are fixed in echo v4.16.3 and later, but the Go vulnerability database doesn't list a fixed v4 version yet, so govulncheck may still report them. Changed The published Docker image is built on Alpine 3.24.4. (#1264) Risks klauspost/compress v1.20.4 is ahead of the v1.18.7 that Server v1.32.2 was tested with. The dev server uses it for zstd compression of Prometheus metrics. The API (go.temporal.io/api v1.63.5) still matches the server. echo v4.16.3 changed Context.RealIP() to ignore cli

entries.text: 💥 Breaking Changes temporal nexus operation describe --output json moves operation fields under info, matching temporal activity describe. The response now has a top-level runId, an info object holding the existing fields, and a top-level input plus either result or failure. Anything parsing the JSON will find execution fields one level down, at .info.operationId instead of .operationId and so on. --raw output also gains the info wrapper. (#1225) temporal worker deployment describe-version --output json leaves out unset times. routingChangedTime, currentSinceTime, rampingSinceTime and drainageInfo (including its lastChangedTime and lastCheckedTime) used to hold 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z or zero-value times when unset; they are now omitted. Scripts that read these fields should treat a missing field as unset. The output also gains status and lastModifierIdentity. (#1223) Highlights This release moves the embedded dev server to OSS Server v1.32.2 and fixes reported vulnerabilities in the CLI's dependencies. Users upgrading from v1.9.1 should read the breaking changes above. Added Standalone Nexus Operations are on by default in the dev server. The CLI sets nexusoperation.enableStandalone=true, which Server v1.32.2 leaves off by default, so every start-dev user now runs this feature. To turn it off, start the dev server with --dynamic-config-value nexusoperation.enableStandalone=false. (#1221) Priority and fairness are visible from the CLI. temporal workflow describe and temporal act

entries.text: 💥 Breaking Changes temporal activity unpause no longer accepts --reset-attempts or --reset-heartbeats. Both flags were no-ops and have been removed; remove them from any scripts, which will otherwise fail on an unknown flag. temporal activity describe returns the full DescribeActivityExecutionResponse, rather than the bare ActivityExecutionInfo. Anything parsing --output json will now encounter execution fields one level down, i.e. at .info.activityId instead of .activityId and so on. The response also adds a top-level runId, which is useful when --run-id was not passed. The command now requests last-failure details, so lastFailure is populated inside info, and text output gains an Activity Execution Info: heading. temporal operator namespace update now requires --active-cluster to be used on its own. Changing the active cluster is a failover operation, so it can no longer be combined with any other namespace update option — configuration changes such as --description, --retention or the archival flags, or --promote-global — and it can no longer be passed empty. Previously these combinations were accepted and silently applied. Split them into two invocations: update the namespace configuration first, then change the active cluster. Connection and output flags such as --namespace and --address are unaffected, and no other flag combination changed.
